subject: literature
passage: For a week, Mateo worked on his grandfather's old radio at the kitchen table. He replaced a cracked wire, cleaned the dusty dials, and tightened every loose screw. <u>Still, when he finally turned the knob, the radio gave only a faint hiss.</u> Mateo sighed and began to pack up his tools. Then his grandfather reached over, tapped the side of the case twice, and music suddenly filled the room.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It describes the first of several repairs that Mateo makes to the radio.
choices.B: It presents a letdown that comes just before the radio suddenly starts to play.
choices.C: It explains why Mateo's grandfather wanted the old radio repaired.
choices.D: It shows that Mateo does not have the skills he would need to repair the radio.

explanation.why: Before the underlined sentence, Mateo has worked for a week on the radio. The underlined sentence, beginning with "Still," tells us his efforts seem to have failed: the radio gives "only a faint hiss." Right after, the grandfather taps the case and "music suddenly filled the room," so the sentence sets up a letdown that the ending reverses.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The repairs are described in the sentence before; the underlined sentence tells what happened after they were finished.
explanation.B: Correct. The sentence describes the apparent failure of Mateo's work, which is then followed by the surprise of the radio playing.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text never says why the grandfather wanted the radio fixed.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The radio does work in the end, and nothing suggests Mateo's repairs were wrong, so this goes further than the text.
